pr_title: [BugFix] Enforce Mistral ToolCall id constraint when using the Mistral tool call parser
pr_body:
This PR introduces a dedicated `MistralToolCall` object (directly inheriting from `ToolCall`) to enforce the random alphanumeric string of size 9 to be used for tool calls parsed with Mistral tool call parser.

FIX #9019

### 🐛 Describe the bug

IDs generated for tool calls parsed by the Mistral parser (flag `--tool-call-parser=mistral`) do not respect the [Mistral ToolCall id naming constraints](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-common/blob/21ee9f6cee3441e9bb1e6ed2d10173f90bd9b94b/src/mistral_common/protocol/instruct/validator.py#L309) and therefore cannot be used in subsequent function call workflow (the error from the [template](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7f60520deb05d2e097b408e3310f1d383fbf1de6/examples/tool_chat_template_mistral.jinja#L79) is raised).

```
ERROR 10-02 05:13:21 serving_chat.py:155] Error in applying chat template from request: Tool call IDs should be alphanumeric strings with length 9!
INFO:     172.17.0.1:59530 - "POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 400 Bad Request
```

comments:
Hi! Yes this is correct - vLLM's standard tool call ID format is incompatible with Mistral's 9-digit (I think?) alphanumeric tool call ID. 

Instead of trying to alter vLLM's internal standard for tool call IDs to be compatible with Mistral, I opted to transform them in the provided chat templates to be compatible with Mistral's format. Details on mistral tool calling & chat templates are [here in the dpcs](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/serving/openai_compatible_server.html#mistral-models)

To resolve this, i recommend using the `examples/tool_chat_template_mistral.jinja` chat template, the `examples/tool_chat_template_mistral_parallel.jinja` chat template, or providing your own that processes vLLM's tool call ID properly.

since before my implementation, tool calls have been generated using the following:

```python
class ToolCall(OpenAIBaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: f"chatcmpl-tool-{random_uuid()}")
    type: Literal["function"] = "function"
    function: FunctionCall
```

I opted not to change this, but it could probably be overridden in the mistral tool parser for anyone who wants to rely on the default mistral chat template.

review_comments: Actually, shouldn't we check that the length is exactly 9?

From my understanding, those tests are common to a lot of different configurations and models.

In particular, the same tests are used for models served with parser other than the mistral parser, and in that case, the tool_call id will be `> 16` (from the [id definition for non mistral tool calls](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/01843c89b8ddae00d4a0f0f56b8aa7fbaa3efc42/vllm/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py#L770))

For the `test_paralllel_tool_call.py` tests, we actually [receive the server config](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/01843c89b8ddae00d4a0f0f56b8aa7fbaa3efc42/tests/tool_use/test_parallel_tool_calls.py#L18) so we could have a check dependant of the parser used, but I opted to have a test that would work both for the mistral parser and other currently defined parsers not to add complexity in the test logic.

What do you think @DarkLight1337 ?
Perhaps we can pass in expected prompt length via test parameters?
If that would be too complicated then I guess the current state is fine.
